title: Rest in God above all (III.21)
hookLine: above all goods and gifts, rest in God
tomorrow: what do you do when the map says no route found?

cards: Health, a good friend, a scholarship, a knee that works again. If God's gifts are good, why rest above them? That's a real question, and two Catholic voices answer it differently.
In chapter twenty-one of book three, the Imitation's disciple empties a whole bag of good things onto the table and asks to rest above every one of them.
Another Catholic voice, older still in its roots, says something that sounds like the opposite.

teach.b: The first voice is the Imitation. Above all things and in all things, the soul tells itself, rest in the Lord. The Latin begins super omnia, above all.
Then the list: above health and beauty, glory and honor, power, knowledge, riches, joy, fame, comfort, hope. Above every gift God can give, and above everything that is not God.
Its reason: whatever God gives apart from himself is too small to satisfy the heart. Its best case is simple.
Gifts can be lost, and a heart that rests only in them has nowhere to stand when they go.
The second voice starts in Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims: "And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good."
Thomas Aquinas built on that, teaching that grace doesn't destroy nature but brings it to its fullness. Its best case: the gifts are how God's goodness reaches you.

Look away from the sunset and the friend to find God, and you may miss where God is showing up. Here's what to tell someone tonight: the Imitation never calls the gifts bad. It calls them too small to lie down in.
And the Church keeps both voices on its shelf, the book that rests above the gifts and the teacher who loves them.

how: Catholics thank God for good things in grace before meals and at night prayer, and many spiritual writers, the Imitation among them, also urge resting the heart in God himself rather than in any gift.

games.q: what does “rest in god above all” mean?
o: rest in God only after your work is finished
take a day off from prayer to rest your mind
rest your heart in God, above even good gifts

s: the Imitation says health and knowledge are bad
it never calls the gifts bad; it calls them too small to rest in.
the Imitation asks to rest even above God's own gifts
above every gift God can give, and everything that is not God.
Catholic teaching sees created things as a distraction from God
Genesis calls them very good, and Aquinas taught that grace brings nature to its fullness.

games.q: your friend loves hiking and says it's where she feels closest to God. a classmate quotes the Imitation: rest above every creature. what's the Imitation side's best case to her?
o: the mountain can be lost; a heart resting only there has nowhere to stand.
nature is a distraction, so she should pray indoors instead.
feeling close to God outdoors is only a mood, not prayer.
games.why: the Imitation never calls the gifts bad. its best case: gifts pass, so rest in the Giver. and her side has Genesis and Aquinas: the gifts are very good.

practice: Count three good things you have right now, one finger at a time, and thank God for each, or simply be glad of it. Then open your hand and let all three rest on your palm without closing around them.

wordCard.voice: Rest in God above all. The Imitation's call to rest above every good gift, because the Giver is the only place big enough to lie down.

orig.note: Latin, Imitation III.21: above all, the chapter's first words for where to rest.

carryVoice: Your line: rest above all. The gifts stay good; they just aren't the bed. Sleep well.
